title: Self Join — Employee and Manager
description: Display each employee with their manager's name using a self join.

data.text: Write a query to display each employee's name alongside their manager's name from the `Employees` table (which has a ManagerID self-referencing foreign key).

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
SELECT
    e.EmployeeID,
    e.FirstName + ' ' + e.LastName AS EmployeeName,
    m.FirstName + ' ' + m.LastName AS ManagerName
FROM Employees e
LEFT JOIN Employees m ON e.ManagerID = m.EmployeeID
ORDER BY e.EmployeeID;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: A self join is when a table is joined to itself. Use different aliases (e for employee, m for manager) to distinguish the two roles. LEFT JOIN ensures the CEO (who has no manager) is still shown with a NULL ManagerName.
